answer: Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so a hostile operator cannot recover it by rotating identities. Forging 341 aliases therefore costs 395 bonds held for 20 days each, plus the kernel attestations those aliases can never earn. A single signal checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Each identity must lock a bond, called a sable, before it can post or attest. That is 37 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
